title: Telemetry-driven canary abort and follow-up: KV cache collision & fallback hardening
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a 10% canary rollout of model vX.3 (quantized LLaMA-variant) we observed an automated canary abort triggered by our new telemetry heuristic. Symptoms were an 8-12x increase in 99th percentile latency for requests that hit cached KV prefixes, elevated tail CPU on GPU-side preprocessors, and a correlated rise in error rates for batched streamed responses. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root-cause analysis, and concrete postmortem actions to harden canary/fallback behavior and update runbooks.
timeline: 2025-02-09T14:02Z - Canary rollout started (10% traffic) for model vX.3
2025-02-09T14:07Z - Synthetic smoke checks passed; gradual ramp continued
2025-02-09T14:21Z - First elevated KV-cache eviction metric spike observed (+420% from baseline)
2025-02-09T14:23Z - Latency 99p increased from 180ms to 1.6s for affected partitions
2025-02-09T14:24Z - Automated telemetry heuristic (kv-collision-tail) crossed threshold and triggered canary abort
2025-02-09T14:25Z - Traffic routed back to prior stable variant; platform returned to normal latency within 30s
2025-02-09T15:00Z - Incident declared; initial notes posted to incident board
2025-02-10T09:00Z - Postmortem review with runtime, infra, and product attended; hypotheses captured
root_causes: KV cache keyspace collision due to new default prefix hashing for trimmed prompts in vX.3 leading to higher local eviction rate
Batching affinity mismatch: new request coalescing logic changed packing for mixed short/long requests increasing average sequence length per batch and exacerbating KV cache pressure
Quantized kernel memory-access pattern in vX.3 interacts poorly with small-batch memory thrash on our target GPU kernel, amplifying tail latency under eviction conditions
Telemetry heuristic was tuned conservatively for throughput anomalies but lacked a short-window correlation with kv-eviction/latency pairing, producing late triggers
mitigations: Reverted rollout (automated by existing rollback path) — immediate mitigation succeeded
Temporarily disabled new prefix-trimming hashing in model load config for all canaries
Throttled canary ramp to 1% for subsequent experiments while we instrument deeper metrics
Updated canary heuristic to require co-occurrence of kv-eviction-rate AND 99p latency within a 60s sliding window to avoid noisy aborts
postmortem_actions: Add KV-key cardinality and per-shard eviction rate to per-canary telemetry (owner: Maria Lopez, due: 2025-02-28)
Implement per-request prefix fingerprint in shadow-mode that does not mutate live traffic but tracks collision frequency (owner: Carlos Nguyen, due: 2025-03-04)
Refine batching affinity config to keep short/long request classes separated in production packing (owner: Rohan Mehta, due: 2025-03-05)
Introduce a 3-stage safety gate: (1) short-window spike; (2) correlated eviction+latency; (3) circuit-breaker cooldown with increasing hysteresis (owner: SRE team, due: 2025-03-10)
Expand canary run to include a 'memory-thrash' synthetic workload that targets quantized kernel paths prior to ramping (owner: QA, due: 2025-03-07)
Document fallback semantics in runbook: explicit note on immediate traffic-swap vs. pause-and-investigate; add checklist to avoid opaque fast rollbacks (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2025-03-01)
acceptance_criteria: New KV-key cardinality metric ingested and visible on per-canary dashboard
Telemetry heuristic updated and covered by unit + e2e tests; false-positive rate reduced in lab runs below 1% for non-failure scenarios
Shadow-mode prefix fingerprinting shows <0.1% collision for baseline workloads OR exposes deterministic pattern to fix
Runbook updated and reviewed by runtime, infra, and SRE; signoff stored in Confluence
runbook_updates: Add step: on canary abort, capture sample of 'eviction-suspect' requests (request IDs and hashed prefix) to avoid missing transient patterns
Add step: run synthetic 'kv-pressure' job to reproduce condition before rollback for 10% traffic canaries
Clarify: automated rollback should include post-rollback verification window of 2 minutes to detect rollback flapping
dashboards_and_alerts: Canary overview dashboard: add 'kv_eviction_rate_per_shard' and 'prefix_collision_rate' panels (Grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/abc123/canary-overview)
Alert: kv-collision-latency — fires when eviction_rate > 3x baseline AND 99p latency > 800ms for 60s
Add notebook for rapid triage that joins traces, kv-eviction, batching affinity, and kernel memory snapshots (notebook link: https://notebooks.redwood.company/p/kv-triage)
code_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4982 - add prefix fingerprinting in shadow path
https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4991 - update canary heuristic to require correlated signals
design_notes: Trade-off considered: stronger heuristic reduces false aborts but increases risk of slow detection for real regressions. We chose a conservative correlated-signal approach with a short cooldown to balance safety and speed.
Considered adding optimistic local-caching on the preprocessor to offload cache pressure; deferred due to complexity and potential staleness issues
